note: If-this-then-that chains that have happened before. Steps with a 'check' light up from the data; steps without one are news to watch for. Likelihoods are best guesses from the history given.

scenarios.title: El Niño dries out Asia's harvests
scenarios.why: The US weather agency (NOAA) says El Niño is still getting stronger. It gives about a 60% chance this becomes the strongest since records began in 1950. Sugar is already up 28% in 3 months. Palm oil is piled up in storage for now, so its rise, if it comes, is more likely in 2027.

steps.text: A strong El Niño forms: the Pacific Ocean runs warm
Dry, hot weather in Indonesia, Malaysia, India, Thailand and Australia
steps.watch: news of drought or weak rainy seasons in those countries

steps.text: Sugar and rice prices climb
Palm oil harvests shrink, and cooking oil jumps 25% or more in a year

scenarios.history: In all 5 strong El Niños since 1990, cooking oil cost more a year later. After the last three, it cost 27% to 55% more.

scenarios.title: La Niña follows and hits the Americas
scenarios.why: La Niña is El Niño's opposite: the Pacific runs cool. After 7 of the 9 strong El Niños since 1950, a La Niña came within 18 months.

steps.text: El Niño peaks and starts to fade
The Pacific flips cool: La Niña
Drought in Argentina, southern Brazil and the southern US
steps.watch: crop news from Argentina and the US Great Plains

steps.text: Soybean or maize prices rise 20% or more in a year

scenarios.history: A La Niña lasted from 2020 to 2023. In its last year, a drought shrank Argentina's soybean harvest to its smallest in over 20 years.

scenarios.title: Expensive oil spreads to food
scenarios.why: Oil alone isn't enough. After 6 big oil jumps since 1990, food was pricier a year later only half the time. Oil is now easing, and world food prices dipped in October. But El Niño could add the second push.

steps.text: Oil jumps
Diesel, shipping and farm costs go up
steps.watch: diesel and shipping prices in the news

steps.text: Crops that get turned into fuel (soybeans, maize, vegetable oil) get pricier
World food prices climb 10% or more in a year

scenarios.history: 2021-22: oil doubled, then Russia invaded Ukraine. World food prices rose 35% in a year, to an all-time high.

scenarios.title: High oil prices fix themselves
scenarios.why: Brent crude fell to about $90 a barrel early this week, far below October's $125 average. Then attacks hit two Saudi refineries and tankers near Iran. By Friday it was back near $97. Gulf oil supply keeps coming back, so this stays likely. But more attacks could flip it.

steps.text: Oil jumps
People drive less, companies cut back, and oil countries pump more
steps.watch: news from OPEC (the big oil countries' group) and talk of a slowdown

steps.text: Oil falls 20% or more from its recent high
Gas, shipping and food get cheaper

down: Copper, if the economy slows a lot
scenarios.history: 2008: oil averaged $134 a barrel in July, then $42 in December when the financial crisis hit. Copper fell by almost two thirds in those months too.

scenarios.title: A ban on food sales sets off a panic
scenarios.why: Governments sometimes stop selling food abroad when it gets expensive at home. Rice and wheat are up sharply this year. India sells about a quarter of the world's rice. It is weighing a tax on rice sold abroad, as its harvests shrink. Russia just banned buckwheat sales abroad. A tax is milder than a ban, so this stays possible.

steps.text: A basic food jumps 25% or more in a year
A big seller stops or limits sales abroad, to keep food cheap at home
steps.watch: India (rice) or Russia (wheat) banning, limiting or taxing sales abroad

steps.text: Buyers panic and prices jump 20% or more in 3 months
Countries that rely on that one seller get hit hardest
steps.watch: the buyers shown in Who feeds whom, below

scenarios.history: 2008: rice nearly tripled in six months after India and Vietnam limited sales. 2010: wheat rose 56% in two months after Russia banned sales. 2023: rice rose 24% in two months after India's ban.

scenarios.title: Cheap fertilizer means bigger harvests
scenarios.why: After 7 big fertilizer price crashes since 1975, maize was cheaper a year later 5 times. This pushes against El Niño and expensive oil.

steps.text: Fertilizer prices crash
Farmers use more fertilizer when they plant in 2027
Bigger harvests
steps.watch: harvest forecasts from the US farm department (USDA) and the UN's food agency (FAO)

steps.text: Grain prices fall 10% or more in 6 months

scenarios.history: Early 2023: fertilizer (urea) had dropped by two thirds from its 2022 high. A year later, maize was 33% cheaper and wheat 26% cheaper.

scenarios.title: A slowdown scare knocks copper down
scenarios.why: Copper briefly fell below $12,000 a tonne on 23 November, after a big drop last week. Doubts about AI spending and weak buying in China are hitting it. But big copper drops are not the usual result of a run-up. After 23 big run-ups since 1960, copper fell 20% within 7 months only 5 times.

steps.text: Copper soars, up 25% or more in a year
Stock markets fall on doubts about AI spending
steps.watch: tech stock news and copper buying in China

steps.text: Copper falls 20% or more from its recent high
If the slowdown spreads, oil and other metals fall too
steps.watch: oil, silver and stock prices in the news

scenarios.history: 2008: copper fell 43% from April to October as the financial crisis hit. 2022: it fell 26% from March to July.
